<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose
   - This is an open-source command-line tool (“Claude Code PM”) for spec-driven project management.  
   - It provides a Claude-powered workflow that turns PRDs into epics, epics into GitHub issues, and issues into code via parallel AI agents.

2. Analyze the file structure
   - Top-level directory: `.claude/` holds all the tool’s configuration and logic.  
     • `agents/` – definitions of AI agents (code-analyzer, file-analyzer, etc.)  
     • `commands/` – markdown definitions of CLI commands (pm, context, testing)  
     • `scripts/` – shell scripts invoked by commands  
     • `context/`, `prds/`, `epics/`, `rules/` – data folders that the tool reads and writes  
   - Supporting files: `AGENTS.md`, `COMMANDS.md`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`  
   - Uses Git (`.gitignore`), GitHub CLI (gh), and a gh-sub-issue extension for issue hierarchies.

3. Examine the README for additional insights
   - The “System Architecture” section already outlines a logical separation:  
     • CLAUDE.md (always-on instructions)  
     • agents, commands, context, epics, prds, rules, scripts  
   - External integrations: GitHub Issues API, Git worktrees, Claude (Anthropic) API.  
   - Core patterns: command-pattern CLI, plugin-style modules (commands, agents), parallel agent orchestration.

4. How to create an accurate system design diagram
   a. Main components
      1. CLI Orchestrator  
         - Entrypoint: `/pm`, `/context`, `/testing`, etc.  
         - Reads command definitions (`.claude/commands/`), invokes scripts and agents  
      2. Local File-store  
         - `.claude/commands/` – command metadata  
         - `.claude/agents/` – agent definitions  
         - `.claude/context/`, `.claude/prds/`, `.claude/epics/`, `.claude/rules/`, `.claude/scripts/`  
      3. AI Agent Manager  
         - Spawns parallel agents (file-analyzer, code-analyzer, test-runner, parallel-worker)  
         - Each agent has its own context window and works in an isolated Git worktree  
      4. Git Integration  
         - Uses Git CLI and worktrees to isolate epics (`git worktree add`)  
         - Commits code and context changes locally  
      5. GitHub Integration  
         - Uses GitHub CLI (`gh`) and gh-sub-issue extension to push epics/tasks as issues  
         - Reads/writes issue comments, labels, and parent-child links  
      6. External AI Service  
         - Calls Claude (Anthropic) API to generate/specify code or analyze context  
   b. Relationships and data flow
      - User invokes a CLI command → CLI Orchestrator  
      - Orchestrator reads `.claude/commands/…` → decides whether to call a script, launch an agent, or sync to GitHub  
      - For “brainstorm” & “parse” phases: calls AI Service via Agent Manager → writes `.claude/prds/` or `.claude/epics/`  
      - For “decompose,” “start,” “sync” phases: Agent Manager spins up parallel agents; each agent reads context from FS, writes updates to FS, commits via Git Integration  
      - For “epic-sync,” “issue-sync,” “import”: CLI uses GitHub Integration to push local markdown → GitHub issues/comments  
   c. Architectural patterns & principles
      - Modular CLI (command-pattern architecture)  
      - Plugin-style modules: commands, agents, scripts, rules  
      - Actor/worker model for parallel AI agents  
      - Spec-driven & traceable: every change maps back to a PRD → epic → task → commit → GitHub issue  
   d. Key technologies & frameworks
      - Node-style module layout (though logic in shell & JS bindings)  
      - Git CLI & worktrees  
      - GitHub CLI (gh) & gh-sub-issue extension  
      - Anthropic Claude API  
      - Markdown files as data store  

5. Guidelines for an open-source CLI tool diagram
   - Emphasize core engine (CLI Orchestrator) at the center  
   - Surround it with plugin modules (commands, agents, rules, scripts)  
   - Show the Local File-store layer as persistent state  
   - Depict two External Services: GitHub API & Claude AI API  
   - Illustrate parallel agent spawning via Agent Manager  
   - Annotate Git Integration (worktrees, commits) between CLI and Git  

6. Diagramming recommendations
   - Use clear labels for each component (e.g., “CLI Orchestrator,” “Agent Manager,” “Commands,” “Scripts,” “Context Store,” “GitHub API,” “Claude API”)  
   - Draw directional arrows for data flow:  
     • User → CLI  
     • CLI ↔ Local FS  
     • CLI → Agent Manager → AI API → Agent Manager → Local FS/Git  
     • CLI → GitHub API  
   - Color-code:  
     • Green boxes for core modules (commands, agents)  
     • Grey box for local filesystem store  
     • Blue for external services (GitHub, Claude)  
     • Orange for Git integration  

7. Essential architectural elements—don't omit
   - Plugin boundaries (commands vs agents vs scripts vs rules)  
   - Parallel worker pattern (multiple agents in isolated worktrees)  
   - Two-way sync with GitHub (issues/comments)  
   - AI service calls abstracted through Agent Manager  

By following these steps, your system diagram will clearly reflect the modular CLI architecture, the local-first file structure, the parallel AI agent orchestration, and the two key external integrations that make “Claude Code PM” work as a transparent, spec-driven project management system.  
</explanation>
